subject: information-technology
intro: Information technology leads to the infrastructure professions — supporting users, keeping networks and servers running, and defending the data those systems hold.

roles.title: Computer User Support Specialists
roles.what: Provide technical assistance to computer users in person, by phone or online, resolving problems with hardware, software, printing, installations, email and operating systems.
roles.where: The types and components of computer systems unit — hardware and software, main components, operating systems — plus input, output and storage devices are the everyday inventory a support specialist troubleshoots.

roles.title: Computer Network Support Specialists
roles.what: Analyse, test, troubleshoot and evaluate network systems — local area networks, wide area networks, cloud networks and servers — performing maintenance that keeps them running with minimal interruption.
roles.where: The Networks and the effects of using them unit, including network issues and communication, is the core knowledge here, sharpened by the Safety and security unit's treatment of how data is protected in transit and at rest.

roles.title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators
roles.what: Install, configure and maintain an organisation's networks, operating systems and physical and virtual servers, monitoring resources, reviewing logs and verifying that scheduled jobs complete correctly.
roles.where: Operating systems and the networks unit teach what an administrator maintains, while the systems life cycle unit — implementation, documentation, evaluation — mirrors the change-management routine of server administration.

roles.title: Information Security Analysts
roles.what: Plan, implement and monitor security measures protecting computer networks and information, assess vulnerabilities, put risk mitigations in place and respond to breaches and malware incidents.
roles.where: The Safety and security unit — eSafety and the security of data — plus the ICT applications unit's banking applications and online communication show where the threats live that analysts spend their careers closing.

roles.title: Web Developers
roles.what: Develop and implement websites, web applications and interactive interfaces, evaluating code for structure and standards and optimising performance, scalability and compatibility across browsers and devices.
roles.where: The practical skills unit's website authoring topic is the direct craft, with the audience unit — audience appreciation and copyright — supplying the design-for-user and legal awareness that professional web work demands.
